reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel σ-algebra, let ν be a probability measure on E × E, let x⋆ ∈ E, let h ∈ ℝ satisfy h ≥ 0, and let M ∈ ℝ. Assume the incoming energy (x,p) ↦ ‖x − x⋆‖² + ‖p‖² is ν-integrable and
∫_{E×E} (‖x − x⋆‖² + ‖p‖²) dν(x,p) ≤ M.
Let γ_E = stdGaussian(E), set μ = ν ⊗ γ_E, and for ((x,p),z) ∈ (E × E) × E define
X((x,p),z) = x,  P₀((x,p),z) = e^(−h/2)p + √(1 − e^(−h)) z.
Then X and P₀ are measurable, the function ((x,p),z) ↦ ‖X((x,p),z) − x⋆‖² + ‖P₀((x,p),z)‖² is μ-integrable, and
∫_{(E×E)×E} (‖X((x,p),z) − x⋆‖² + ‖P₀((x,p),z)‖²) dμ((x,p),z)
= ∫_{E×E} (‖x − x⋆‖² + e^(−h)‖p‖²) dν(x,p) + (1 − e^(−h)) finrank_ℝ(E)
≤ M + (1 − e^(−h)) finrank_ℝ(E).
objects: E; the incoming probability law ν; the reference point x⋆; the nonnegative refresh length h; the energy bound M; the standard Gaussian law γ_E; the product law μ; and the coordinate maps X and P₀.
domains: E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure; ν is a probability measure on E × E; x⋆ lies in E; h and M are real numbers with h ≥ 0; μ is a probability measure on (E × E) × E; and X and P₀ map (E × E) × E into E.
quantifiers: Universally quantified over E, ν, x⋆, h, and M, subject to the stated structural, probability, nonnegativity, integrability, and energy-bound hypotheses.
assumptions: E is complete, finite-dimensional, real inner-product, and Borel; ν is an incoming probability law on E × E; h ≥ 0; the incoming energy (x,p) ↦ ‖x − x⋆‖² + ‖p‖² is ν-integrable; and its ν-integral is at most M.
conclusion: Under μ = ν ⊗ stdGaussian(E), both X((x,p),z)=x and P₀((x,p),z)=e^(−h/2)p+√(1−e^(−h))z are measurable. Their combined squared energy is μ-integrable, its integral is exactly the incoming position energy plus e^(−h) times the incoming momentum energy plus (1−e^(−h))finrank_ℝ(E), and this is at most M+(1−e^(−h))finrank_ℝ(E).
scopes: The incoming integrability assumption and bound are taken over E × E with respect to ν. The refreshed energy, measurability statements, exact identity, and final inequality are taken over (E × E) × E with respect to μ = ν ⊗ stdGaussian(E). The Gaussian coordinate z is fresh and independent of the incoming pair (x,p).
constant_dependencies: The additive Gaussian contribution depends only on h and the real dimension finrank_ℝ(E). The final upper bound additionally depends on M. No further constant depends on ν, x⋆, x, p, or z.
